biggest_catch: Pay is per audio minute, not per work minute — transcribing 60 minutes of audio typically takes 3-4 hours of real work, so effective hourly pay is modest; work is graded and low grades lose access, plus a current application waitlist.
catches: Pay is per audio/video minute, not per minute worked — difficult audio eats far more time than it pays.

Work availability varies; no guaranteed volume or income.
You handle your own taxes as an independent contractor.

maximize: Pass the skills assessment and sample on the first try by studying Rev's style guide — a clean start avoids grading penalties. Claim short, single-speaker, clear-audio files first: they take ~25-35 minutes per 15 audio minutes, maximizing your effective rate. Maintain high grades by following formatting rules exactly — cumulative grades control access to higher-paying files, so never rush sloppy work. Once qualified, add captioning ($0.54-$1.10/min) which pays slightly more than transcription. Payments arrive automatically every Monday via PayPal for the prior week's approved work — no invoice needed.

steps: Apply at rev.com/freelancers and choose the transcriptionist role.
Pass the English/grammar skills assessment and the sample transcription.
Claim files from the work queue — start with short, clear single-speaker audio.
Transcribe accurately following Rev's style guide (speaker labels, formatting).
Submit before the file deadline; graded work is approved and paid.
Payment arrives the following Monday via PayPal for the week's approved work.
timing: Paid weekly via PayPal for all approved work (previous week's work).

work_available: Open work queue, but availability varies — you claim files as they post, with no guaranteed volume or income; a current application waitlist may delay your start.
